short: A decisive Swedish victory over a larger Polish-Saxon army during Charles XII's Polish campaign.
full:
The Battle of Kliszów took place on 19 July 1702, during the early years of the Great Northern War. A Swedish army under Charles XII, numbering about 12,000 men, faced a combined Saxon and Polish-Lithuanian force of over 24,000 commanded by Augustus II the Strong. Despite being heavily outnumbered, the Swedes executed a successful flanking maneuver.

The Swedish forces shattered the Saxon center and forced the allied army into a chaotic retreat, capturing their artillery and camp. The victory secured Swedish control over much of Poland, allowing Charles XII to depose Augustus II and install his preferred candidate, Stanisław Leszczyński, on the Polish throne.
